data.content_ref: inline:Artifact 18174034ea0c contradicts artifact 2f8f85328fae on the locus of the correctness obligation for deterministic replay in an append-only log: 18174034ea0c asserts the writer must be idempotent, while 2f8f85328fae asserts the writer need only append and the consumer's fold operation must be commutative (duplicate-suppressing). They share a mechanism—duplicate suppression—but allocate it to different components. The contradiction is sharpened by 3fc33b3603be's formal definition of idempotency as f(f(x))=f(x), which 18174034ea0c applies to the writer while 2f8f85328fae effectively relocates to the fold. This is refuted if the two positions are equivalent reformulations rather than competing allocations—i.e., if writer-level idempotency and consumer-level fold commutativity always co-occur as jointly necessary and sufficient conditions, making the disagreement merely notational rather than substantive.
